opportunities.query_text: Amplemarket wants to replace your SDR stack with one AI copilot... The Startup plan is $600 a month for two seats, billed annually, with no monthly option and no published free trial anywhere on the site. Fifteen thousand email credits and 480 phone credits per user come with it... Growth and Elite are both custom quotes, & neither publishes a number. Vendr's tracked-contract data puts the real median at $16,608 a year, ranging from $11,678 to $35,946. That's two to five times the advertised Startup rate, once a team needs the tiers Amplemarket won't price in public. Has anyone here signed a Growth or Elite contract? I'd like to know if the number landed near that $16,608 median.

opportunities.query_text: Uber burned its entire 2026 AI budget in four months, and had to cut back on usage. Agentic AI cost just doesn't behave like traditional software that we know how to budget for. I spent years at Apptio building the tooling that made cloud spend predictable, and that playbook doesn't survive contact with agents. Most teams are learning that lesson the hard way. My new piece is on why agentic AI keeps blowing out of budget, and what makes it so hard to see coming. Would like to hear from others how they are managing their AI costs.

summary: Fourth consecutive thin run, and the run that found the monitor's real defect. Supply is not the problem: 1,044 requests carry a lastmod since 2026-09-02 and 164 bodies were text-scanned this run, yet only one on-beat request is under a week old and it is a near-miss (Inc.'s US-founders callout, fresh and top-tier but asking for a firsthand account we cannot give). The important finding is not about supply — it is that the queue was lying about age. build_pitch_queue.py derived a request's age from the digest's deadline text and, whenever that text carried no date, fell back to the digest's first-seen date. Four requests were affected: a 2026-03-10 request showing as 8 days old, a 2026-05-22 request as 7 days, a 2026-03-16 request as 7 days, and a 2026-08-24 request as 7 days. Two of those were sitting at the top of the 'Live - pitch these' list. Ages are now read off each page's datePublished, cached in verified-requests.json and refreshed by scripts/verify_journo_requests.py; the builder also dedupes the www./non-www. duplicate URL, and no longer labels any route 'automatable'. Real live queue: 9 requests under 10 days, of which the on-beat ones are 9-11 days and absent from the live feed, and the 0-day ones are off-beat. The single most sendable on-beat request is the Amplemarket pricing-opacity piece, because its page links to a site that publishes a working contact address (contact@marketintelligencetools.com, MX verified) - and it must be answered as a method-and-data contribution, not as a Growth/Elite customer, which we are not. The one pitch sent so far (2026-09-15, to Fox + Spindle) has had no reply as of this run. Access is unchanged: HARO and Connectively both behind a Vercel checkpoint at HTTP 429 (sixth run), Qwoted needs an authenticated session, Source of Sources is reporter-only, MentionMatch is a pre-launch shell, X is credit-blocked, and Medialyst still needs the OAuth handshake that cron cannot complete.

monitor_health.extractor_check_this_run: PASSED, with one correction. Two traps confirmed: (1) the string 'has been removed or is no longer available' and the word 'expired' both appear in Sourcee's JS bundle on EVERY page including valid ones - a 2026-09-16 attempt to detect removal that way flagged all 13 live requests as expired. Detect removal by an empty rendered body, not by keyword. (2) The single request object sits in the escaped RSC flight payload; datePublished, headline and domain are all recoverable by regex, and `domain` is how the publishing outlet is identified (inc.com, theguardian.com, sciencemag.org, industrydive.com, marketintelligencetools.com). The rendered badge is the authoritative freshness wording.
known_traps: Digest `deadline` text is prose, not data. 'Open (posted >1 month ago)' carries no parseable date, so any age derived from it silently falls back to the digest's first-seen date. Age must come from the page. Fixed this run.
The sitemap lastmod is a re-index timestamp as well as a post timestamp; a recent lastmod is not a recent post. Check datePublished.
Slug-token matching is not evidence. This run's false positives included 'fee' on an eVisa story, 'spend' on Indian festive retail, and 'budget' on a personal-finance post. The body fetch decides.
Outlet pages (/media-outlets/<slug>/journo-requests) are persistent ~20-item lists, not rolling feeds; absence is not proof of expiry.
The same request appears in digests with and without the www. host - dedupe on the canonical URL or the queue lists it twice.
Absence from a single digest is weak evidence: the 2026-09-15 digest carried only 2 opportunities because the monitor chose not to carry more, which is not the same as the feed dropping them.
